analysis:
Examined all units. Test/golden changes: gemma-4-26b.json adds a routedExperts block (loadedBytes 24265359360, 128 experts, 8 selected), and expected.json updates three Gemma plan and hand-off hashes, which is consistent with the layout change. Main.swift only registers a new check, checkGemmaRoutedExperts. All three are test-only and add no runtime attack surface. The new check's implementation is not in this batch. The mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moves from 7933a0f to 3c01ffc. Its content is not supplied, so I cannot assess the inference engine, KV cache or media handling it contains (TB-007, T-041, T-050). A pointer bump is routine but the new submodule code needs its own review.

The security-relevant runtime change is in DistributedInstalledPlan.swift. defaultBatchLanes now returns gemma4PipelineBatchLanes = 4 for Gemma 4 layer-stage pipelines with serial prefill and no private images. The old default was 1 lane. The doc comments say each lane is charged its full request state on every rank, is admitted against live memory, and is refused retryably if it does not fit. That admission code is not in the supplied evidence. The change affects availability and the A-018 memory-pressure surface, and it also bears on consumer-isolation assumptions for concurrent requests (A-001), because the lanes share a model and KV state. The comments assert per-row arithmetic isolation (Gemma4BatchDecodeScope, Gemma4BatchArithmeticAgreement), but that is not verifiable here. Private-image requests (hasPrivateImages) are excluded and still fall through to the previous behavior. The lookahead schedule and nil schedule stay at 1 lane. The owner's environment override still applies, and a malformed override is documented to fall back to 1 lane.

Open questions for integration: (1) whether the lane admission and memory accounting really refuse a lane the host cannot hold, so that 4 lanes do not cause OOM or DoS; (2) whether the cross-request isolation of KV and prefix-cache state (the cacheSalt scoping from T-041) holds under 4 concurrent Gemma pipeline lanes; (3) the new mlx-swift-lm submodule contents. No concrete regression is demonstrable from the supplied evidence.
